newsitem.title: INDIA: India raises 97/98 petroleum demand to 90.87 mln T.
newsitem.headline: India raises 97/98 petroleum demand to 90.87 mln T.

text.p: The Indian government has increased its estimate of the nation's demand for petroleum products in 1997/98 (April/March) to 90.87 million tonnes from 88.18 million, an Oil Coordination Committee (OCC) official said on Wednesday.
"Imports, which had been pegged at 24.98 million tonnes this year, are expected to go up by 2.69 million to 27.67 million," the official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
The demand and import estimates have been adjusted following the revision of economic growth projections.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram is forecasting annual growth of gross domestic product (GDP) of seven percent for the ninth five-year plan period from 1997 to 2002, the official said.
The previous demand projection of 88.18 million tonnes had been prepared in August 1996 and assumed annual GDP growth of 6.5 percent over the next five years, he said.
"The new demand and import estimates will be realised provided the finance minister achieves the seven percent growth rate. So far, figures point to the contrary," the OCC official said.

Another factor which is expected to boost demand is use of naphtha in power plants. Naphtha demand in 1997/98 is expected to total 9.74 million tonnes, up from an earlier estimate of 6.33 million, he said.

The estimate of 1997/98 demand includes allocations of naphtha, fuel oil and low sulphur heavy stock made during the last three years. These allocations were excluded from the August 1996 estimate, he said.

The latest estimate includes substitute fuels for natural gas-based projects which could fall short of supplies. It also includes demand for fuel and feedstock by new and expanded fertiliser and petrochemical projects, he added.
The OCC, set up in 1975 to administer the oil pool account and set monthly production, is part of the Petroleum Ministry.
